record.paper_title: String Theory on ADS3: Some Open Questions
record.original_question: What is the physical and modular meaning of the source or magnetic field v coupled to J3_0 in SU(1,1) Wess–Zumino–Witten characters, and can it be interpreted as a continuous twist whose summation restores modular invariance in analogy with parafermionic constructions or the two-dimensional Euclidean black hole?

evidence.quote: In our formal treatment, the only way out is to lift the degeneracy by switching on a source coupled to J3_0.
the above models are only defined in the presence of a ‘magnetic field’, which is not invariant under modular transformations. The interpretation of these features is not clear.

In particular, the role of the ‘magnetic field’ v remains obscure. The possibility of interpreting it as a continuous twist, similar to those that appear in the parafermionic constructions, has never been exploited.
One might, though, relax in this way the constraint of modular invariance: the latter should be recovered only after an appropriate summation over v.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the level-$k$ Wess–Zumino–Witten model based on the non-compact group $SU(1,1)\cong SL(2,\mathbb R)$. Because the Cartan generator $J^3_0$ has a continuous, unbounded spectrum on the unitary representations (principal continuous, discrete highest/lowest weight, and their spectral-flow images), the naive characters $\chi(\tau)=\mathrm{Tr}\,q^{L_0-c/24}$ are divergent and degenerate, and one is forced to introduce a regulator by coupling a "magnetic field" $v\in\mathbb C$ to $J^3_0$, defining
$$\chi(\tau,v)\;=\;\mathrm{Tr}\Bigl(e^{2\pi i v J^3_0}\,q^{L_0-c/24}\Bigr).$$
These regulated characters carry a well-defined action of the modular group only when $v$ is transformed nontrivially, and for fixed $v\neq 0$ the resulting torus partition function fails to be modular invariant.

(a) Give an intrinsic physical interpretation of the parameter $v$: in particular, determine whether $v$ can be consistently understood as a continuous holonomy / twist of the $U(1)$ subgroup generated by $J^3$ around one of the cycles of the worldsheet torus, in analogy with the continuous twists used in parafermionic coset constructions and in the $SL(2,\mathbb R)/U(1)$ two-dimensional Euclidean black hole.

(b) Assuming such an interpretation, decide whether modular invariance of the SL(2,R) WZW partition function can be recovered by an appropriate integration (or summation) over $v$ together with a conjugate variable, and exhibit the measure and contour that achieve this, producing a modular invariant partition function with the correct spectrum of unitary representations (including spectral flow sectors).
artifact.category_tag: SL(2,R) WZW characters and modular invariance
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Maldacena, Ooguri and Schwimmer (hep-th/0001063) and Maldacena–Ooguri Part 2 (hep-th/0005183) computed the one-loop partition function of strings on thermal AdS_3 / Euclidean BTZ and showed that the regulator coupled to J^3_0 is naturally identified with a chemical potential / continuous holonomy of the timelike U(1)⊂SL(2,R) around the torus cycles. Modular invariance is achieved by treating this variable on the same footing as τ and integrating over it with the appropriate non-holomorphic measure, producing a modular invariant Z(τ,τ̄;u,ū) and reproducing the SL(2,R) spectrum including spectral flow. The interpretation as a continuous twist analogous to parafermionic / 2d Euclidean black hole constructions is thus confirmed.

status_evidence.title: Modular invariance of string theory on AdS_3
status_evidence.snippet: We construct a modular invariant partition function for strings on AdS_3 in terms of characters of SL(2,R), introducing an additional variable u that plays the role of a chemical potential for J^3_0.
status_evidence.claim: The 'magnetic field' v is identified with a chemical potential/holonomy and modular invariance is restored by including it together with τ.

status_evidence.title: Strings in AdS_3 and the SL(2,R) WZW Model. Part 2: Euclidean Black Hole
status_evidence.snippet: We compute the one-loop partition function for Euclidean BTZ (thermal AdS_3) backgrounds, which is modular invariant and from which one can read off the spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: The thermal AdS_3 partition function is modular invariant and interprets the regulator as a holonomy of the timelike U(1) around worldsheet cycles.
